items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6351

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electronic
bell jar games

 
PURPOSE:

To authorize the use of electronic- bell jar vending machines by author-
ized charitable organizations.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Establishes legislative, findings and purpose.

Section 2: Authorizes and defines electronic bell jar vending machines
for the purpose of conducting bell jar games.

Section 3: Prohibits any electronic bell jar vending machine from being
sold, leased, distributed, installed, or operated until approved by the
New York State Gaming Commission.

Section 4: Prohibits any charitable organization from purchasing or
leasing any electronic bell jar vending machine from any manufacturer or
distributor that is not licensed by New York State Gaming Commission.

Section 3: Establishes the license fee for manufacturers of electronic
bell jar vending machines.

Section 6: Establishes the operational requirements for electronic bell
jar vending machines.

Section 7: Prohibits any manufacturer from selling any electronic bell
jar vending machine to any distributor that is net licensed by the New
York State Gaming Commission; and requires manufacturers to report to
the York State Gaming Commission any Electronic bell jar vending machine
sold or leased to a distributor.

Section 8: Prohibits any distributor from purchasing any electronic bell
jar vending machine from any manufacturer that is not licensed by the
New York State Gaming Commission; and requires distributors to maintain
records of all electronic bell jar vending machines that sell or leases
and to report such information to the New York State Gaming Commission.

Section 9: Establishes additional requirements and compliance standards
for electronic bell jar vending machines. This section also limits the
number of electronic bell jar vending machines that an authorized organ-
ization may *operate to no more than five machines.  Additionally, this
section provides that an authorized organization must be licensed to
operate games of chance prior to the effective date Of this legislation
and offer bell jar games to be authorized to Operate electronic, bell
jar vending machines unless they are a specified veterans organization:
Finally, this section prohibits any *operation of electronic tell jars
in the identified exclusivity zone.

Section 10: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill seeks to provide a pure entertainment form of a "bell jar"
vending machine that has been a. popular fundraising device for charita-
ble and fraternal organizations. The electronic form of this vending
machine will also inhibit the purchase of illegal bell jar tickets and
the manipulation of the outcome bell jar games and provide state-of-the-
art accounting devices that will provide regulators with assurances that
bell jar games are conducted in accordance with law.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

NOR

2019-20: S.6281- REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

2020-21: S.284- REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

2021-22: S.1440- REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

2022-23: S.1440- REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

2023-24: S.1959- REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Potential for enhanced revenues to the state 'through licensing fees and
from charitable gaming.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on January 1, 2026.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6351B

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electronic
bell jar games

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To authorize the use of electronic bell jar vending machines by author-
ized charitable organizations.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Establishes legislative findings and purpose.

Section 2: Authorizes and defines electronic bell jar vending machines
for the purpose of conducting bell jar games.

Section 3: Requires that electronic bell jar vending machines be
approved by the New York State Gaming Commission prior to being sold,
leased, distributed, installed, or operated.

Section 4: Prohibits charitable organizations from purchasing or leasing
electronic bell jar vending machines from any person or organization
other than those licensed as suppliers by the New York State Gaming
Commission.

Section 5: Establishes the license fee for manufacturers of electronic
bell jar vending machines.

Section 6: Establishes various operational, display, and technological
requirements for electronic bell jar vending machines, and sets limita-
tions on the number of machines an authorized organization may operate
based on membership levels and proximity to other gaming facilities.

Section 7: Prohibits any manufacturer from selling any electronic bell
jar vending machine to any distributor that is not licensed by the New
York State Gaming Commission and requires manufacturers to report to the
Commission on the sale or lease of such machines.

Section 8: Prohibits any distributor from purchasing any electronic bell
jar vending machine from any manufacturer that is not licensed by the
New York State Gaming Commission; requires distributors and manufactur-
ers to obtain Commission approval for contracts or agreements related to
the sale, lease, or distribution of such machines to authorized organ-
izations; and authorizes the Gaming Commission to promulgate related
rules and regulations.

Section 9: Establishes additional requirements for the operation of
electronic bell jar vending machines, including premises restrictions
and the need for specific authorization from the Commission.

Section 10: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


This bill seeks to modernize a popular and profitable fundraising mech-
anism utilized by charitable and fraternal organizations, including but
not limited to veterans organizations, across the state. By authorizing
the use of electronic bell jar vending machines, this bill would allow
such organizations to increase charitable gaming revenues and attract
new members, mirroring the technological advancements seen in other
areas of the gaming landscape. The electronic form of this game will
enhance integrity by providing state-of-the-art accounting and tracking
features, ensuring that the games are conducted in accordance with all
applicable rules and regulations, and allowing charitable organizations
to more efficiently manage their bell jar offerings. The bill includes
appropriate safeguards to ensure these devices remain a limited and
controlled fundraising tool, distinct in form and function from other
gaming devices.

Potential for enhanced revenues to the state through licensing fees and
from charitable gaming.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 74 Chapter 697
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 6351-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electron-
        ic bell jar games"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would allow any authorized organization to utilize electron-
ic  bell  jar  machines.  Bell  jar games are a means of fundraising for
numerous charitable organizations. Electronic bell jar machines offer  a
new, updated method of play for this charitable fundraising game.
 
  As  written,  the  expansive  scope of this bill would have led to the
potential proliferation of  bell  jar  machines  throughout  the  state,
including  in  close  proximity to tribal and commercial casinos. I have
reached an agreement with the legislature to ensure that our state  does
not  become  over saturated, by permitting them to be cited by volunteer
firefighters and veterans' organizations that  are  existing  licensees.
Based upon that agreement, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
